project.name: Crowland Historic Town Explorer

properties.name: Crowland curated visitor boundary
properties.methodology: Morphological closing of the preserved official built-up-area geometry using a 150 metre outward and inward buffer. This fills internal omissions for connected parks, river corridors and visitor green spaces without applying a general outward town buffer.

project.boundarySource: Curated Crowland visitor boundary derived from ONS Built-up Areas (December 2024)
project.researchNotes: Townscape Guides audit completed 2026-08-09. The unchanged ONS 2024 built-up area is the active inclusion boundary. Historic England designations and public current OpenStreetMap visitor facilities were filtered point-in-polygon.

touristAppeal.label: Local detour
touristAppeal.summary: Crowland qualifies as a local detour through Crowland Abbey and Trinity Bridge. It is best treated as a shorter stop rather than a half-day destination.

townGuide.headline: A great abbey, a three-way bridge and deep Fenland history
townGuide.intro: The Abbey supplies scale and atmosphere, Trinity Bridge is a genuine curiosity, and the town’s sculpture and waterways explain a settlement once surrounded by marsh.
perfectFor: Small in scale but distinctive enough to reward a purposeful detour.

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Crowland Abbey and Trinity Bridge
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Start at the Abbey, walk into the centre for Trinity Bridge and the Arrival sculpture, then add the wildlife pond.

dontMiss: Crowland Abbey (St Mary & St Bartholomew & St Guthlac)
townGuide.visitorMood: Small in scale but distinctive enough to reward a purposeful detour.
